name: Mung bean cleansing

lead: Ground mung bean was used in early Korean cosmetics as a cleanser. According to a Wikipedia overview of Korean cosmetics, it contains saponin, a natural foaming compound, and was helpful for cleansing [1].
The practice is cited in K-beauty as a traditional, plant-based approach to washing the face and keeping skin looking clean.

paras: Detailed traditional preparation is not described in the encyclopedia source [1]. Mung beans themselves are a widely eaten legume in Korea, China, South Asia and Southeast Asia [2].
No safety information is given in the sources. As with any powder applied to skin, individuals can react to plant ingredients.

chain: Saponin helps lift dirt and oil
angle.text: Mung bean powder was used as a face wash: its saponin content gave a mild cleansing action, supporting a clean skin appearance.

lead: Mung bean cleansing is a traditional Korean skin-cleansing practice in which ground mung bean was used as a cleanser. Wikipedia's overview of Korean cosmetics lists ground mung bean among early plant-based ingredients, noting that it contains saponin and was helpful for cleansing [1].

The mung bean was domesticated in India and spread to China and Southeast Asia; in Korea it is eaten in pancakes, jelly and sprouts [2]. Its use as a cleanser is a cosmetic application of a familiar food crop.
Appearance-wise, the aim is cleaner, clearer-looking skin through a gentle plant-based wash. The topic is documented only briefly.

paras: Early Korean cosmetics were made from plant-derived lotions, including gourd stems, and camellia and castor oils were used on hair; ground mung bean served for cleansing because of its saponin [1].
The mung bean was domesticated in India, with carbonized beans at archaeological sites suggesting cultivation roughly 4,000 to 4,500 years ago, and spread to China and Southeast Asia [2].
